en.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 Hunter Class Freezes and Shatters Xenomorphs
en.summary: Prepare for a new wave of terror as Cold Iron Studios unveils the Hunter class for Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2. This versatile operative brings crowd control and devastating damage to the Xenomorph-infested battlefields.
en.body:
The relentless Xenomorph threat in **Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2** is about to get a whole lot more manageable, or perhaps even more terrifying, depending on your perspective. Developer Cold Iron Studios has lifted the lid on the game's Hunter class, showcasing a specialist designed to control the flow of battle and deliver decisive blows.

The Hunter's core identity revolves around its unique Particle Pulse ability, a versatile tool that can be modified to serve two distinct purposes. Players can opt for the Particle Beam, unleashing a torrent of energy to decimate approaching hordes of Xenomorphs. Alternatively, they can switch to the Cryo Pulse, a chilling modification that freezes enemies in their tracks. While this might sound like a purely supportive role, don't underestimate its offensive potential. Frozen Xenomorphs are far easier targets, and as the latest trailer demonstrates, a well-placed shot can shatter them into icy fragments, turning their frozen state into their final moments.

For those who prefer a different approach to enemy manipulation, the Hunter also wields the Stasis Bolt. This ability slows down enemies, making them easier to hit and more vulnerable to follow-up attacks. Its upgrade paths, Vlad Bolt and Arc Bolt, further enhance its debuffing capabilities, ensuring that no Xenomorph can easily escape the Hunter's grasp. Complementing these active abilities are the Hunter's unique perks: No Mercy and No Rest. Both are designed to significantly increase damage output, with one focusing on raw stopping power and the other on weapon damage. However, to truly capitalize on these perks, players will need to demonstrate pinpoint accuracy, as the damage boosts are exclusively tied to hitting enemy weak points.

## Mastering the Hunt

This new class isn't just about abilities; it's also about the tools of the trade. The Hunter can choose from two signature weapons that perfectly complement its playstyle. The BD-03 Djinn Personal Railgun offers a respectable accuracy rating of 86 and stability of 74, with its damage beginning to taper off around the 60-meter mark. For players demanding absolute precision, the Type 111 Directed Particle Emitter boasts a perfect accuracy rating of 100. This weapon, combined with the Hunter's perks, promises unparalleled precision damage against the alien menace.

The Hunter class embodies the core tenets of the **Aliens** universe: adaptability and the will to survive against overwhelming odds. Its toolkit allows players to either become an unstoppable force of destruction or a crucial linchpin for team survival, dictating the pace of combat and ensuring that the Xenomorphs never get the upper hand. This flexibility is key to the co-op strategy that **Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2** is built upon.

## What's Next for Fireteam Elite

With the **Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2** release date set for August 25, 2026, the continued reveals of its diverse classes like the Hunter are building considerable anticipation. Fans are eager to see how these new mechanics and character archetypes will integrate into the expanded co-op gameplay. The promise of enhanced strategies and deeper team synergy suggests that Cold Iron Studios is delivering a robust and engaging experience for both veteran players and newcomers to the franchise.

content_raw: As we get closer to the August 25th release of co-op shooter Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 , developer Cold Iron Studios has revealed more details about the game’s Hunter class . The details are accompanied by a trailer that showcases the class’s various abilities as well as the special tools players can use to support their team. Check it out below. The class is designed around the Particle Pulse ability, which can further be modified into either a Particle Beam or a Cryo Pulse. While the former can be used to dish out massive damage to incoming hordes of Xenomorphs, the latter can instead be used to provide support by freezing enemies in place. Don’t mistake the supportive potential of the Cryo Pulse for a lack of damage, however. Frozen enemies are easier to kill, after all, and as the trailer showcases, players can simply shatter the frozen enemies by shooting them with their weapon of choice. Players not interested in Particle Pulse can instead look forward to using the Stasis Bolt, which slows down enemies and makes them vulnerable through its two upgrade choices: Vlad Bolt and Arc Bolt. These core tools are supported by the Hunter’s unique perks – No Mercy and No Rest. Both revolve around increasing damage dealt, with one focused on raw stopping power and the other on weapon damage. However, to make full use of these perks, players will need to make sure that their shots are accurate, since the damage boosts only apply to weak points. The Hunter gets to choose from two signature weapons: the BD-03 Djinn Personal Railgun and the Type 111 Directed Particle Emitter. The former boasts an accuracy rating of 86 and a stability rating of 74, with its damage starting to fall off at around the 60-meter mark. The latter has a perfect accuracy rating of 100 and a stability rating of 87. Interestingly, it seems to have infinite range, with no damage falloff at all. For the purposes of balance, however, it would be safe to assume that the Type 111 Directed Particle Emitter likely offers more limited uses when compared to the BD-03 Djinn Personal Railgun. Cold Iron Studios has showcased three of the other classes before – the Marauder , the Specialist , and the Machinist . The Specialist focuses on adding versatility to any given group thanks to its ability to mix and match between other classes. However, the downside is that the class has unique unlock requirements. The Machinist gives players access to high-damage plasma-based weapons that can help any group tear through hordes of Xenomorphs. Its drones and turrets can also help when it comes to controlling the battlefield. Finally, the Marauder has been described as a “force multiplier” for the group thanks to its rocket launchers, concussive grenades, and other destructive tools. Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.
